name: Sultans of Dehli, D0025var, Taj al-Din Yildiz, AR Dirham, Ghanza
zeno_description: Delhi Sultanate, Taj al -Din Yildiz, ‘Silver Multiple Unit’ Dirham In The Name Of His Former Master Muhammad BIn Sam (Baldat Ghazna Mint) Ruler : Taj al -Din Yildiz Era : (AH 602-612 / 1206-1215 AD) Dynasty : Turks Mint : Baldat Ghazna Mint Denomination : Silver Multiple Unit Weight : 8.81 g Diameter : 29.80 mm Reference : G&G D25 Obverse : Within double square, ‘Al-sultan Al-azam mui'zz al-dunya wa-aldin abu'l muzaffar Muhammad Bin Sam’ name and title of Taj al-Din Yildiz in margin 'Taj al-dunya Wal'din Yildiz al-sultani Abdahu maulah'. Reverse : Within double square, 'Kalima and title "al-Nasir li-din Allah Amir al-Mumineen" in four lines, Mint name 'Baldat Ghazna' in right margin date in words around. Comment : The titles used for Taj al -Din Yildiz are 'Abdahu maulah' means 'Slave of lord' (protector) it is used in various parts of the Islāmic world as an honorific attached to the name of a king, sultan, or other noble, This rare Dirham was strucked by Yildiz in the name of his deceased master Mu’izz al-Din Muhammad Bin Sam (Muhammad Ghori). This Dirham is heavier (8.81) grams as compared to the standard weight Dirhams (5.01 g). This denomination is in between Dirham and Double Dirham. Very Rare.
